title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD & roadmap, pricing notes, and Q4 release notes
author: Priya Patel
summary: Comprehensive product document covering Unified Inference: high-level overview, prioritized PRD and requirements, design constraints, roadmap and themes for next two quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and the Q4 release notes and rollout plan.
body:
Purpose

This page consolidates product-level artifacts for Unified Inference: a single reference for engineering, go-to-market, and customer-facing teams. It includes the product overview, prioritized PRD and acceptance criteria, key design constraints, roadmap and themes for the next two quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and the Q4 release notes and rollout plan. Use this page as the canonical source when preparing release communications, sales enablement, and internal launch readiness.

1) Product overview

Executive summary:
- Unified Inference is Redwood’s flagship product that provides a single API and operational model to serve LLM workloads across Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Goal: make inference predictable and economical while preserving developer ergonomics and production SLAs.

Key capabilities (high-level):
- Multi-mode deployment: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private VPC package.
- Routing and fallback: policy-based routing (latency, cost, region, tier) with automatic variant fallback.
- Cost/perf controls: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles, and model variant recommendations.
- Observability & operations: per-route telemetry, token-level cost, regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

Primary personas and use-cases:
- ML engineer: optimizing throughput/latency for high-volume inference workloads.
- Product engineer: embedding/generation features with consistent latency and cost.
- Platform team: standardizing inference across multiple business units and regions.

2) PRD and prioritized requirements

Overview and success metrics (OKRs):
- Objective: Increase adoption of Dedicated and Private modes by mid-market and enterprise accounts while reducing hosted per-token cost by 20% for heavy request patterns using Optimize recommendations.
- Key results: (1) 30% growth in Dedicated ARR in Q1; (2) average tail latency P95 <= 120ms for 4k token horizon on common model families; (3) Reduce token cost for top 10 customers by 18% via Optimize suggestions.

Problem statement:
Customers want one consistent API with predictable SLAs and a straightforward upgrade path from Hosted to Dedicated/Private without re-architecting their integrations. They also need cost controls and deterministic performance across traffic patterns.

Top-level requirements (MUST/SHOULD/CAN):
1. MUST: Single stable REST/SDK contract for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking across deployment modes.
2. MUST: Policy-based routing engine with per-customer override rules and automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
3. MUST: Observability: per-request token counts, cost attribution, latency breakdowns (scheduling, kernel execution, packaging).
4. MUST: Model pinning and rollout primitives (canary, A/B, automatic rollback) integrated with config APIs.
5. SHOULD: Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching, caching, and quantization with expected delta estimates (latency/cost/quality).
6. SHOULD: Out-of-the-box quantized model profiles (INT8/FP16) with validated latency & quality metrics.
7. CAN: Offline packaging for on-prem installs with minimal manual steps (airgap-friendly artifact set).

Acceptance criteria (example - routing engine):
- Policy rules can be created via UI and API; a route change propagates to the control plane within 30s.
- At least two fallback strategies: model-variant fallback and region fallback; both exercised in integration tests.
- Unit/regression tests for routing must cover 95% of rule permutations in simulation harness.

3) Design specs and constraints

Design principles:
- Production-first: prioritize predictable latencies, observability, and fail-safe fallbacks.
- Developer-first: keep API surface minimal and stable across releases.
- Cost-awareness: expose knobs and recommended defaults rather than opaque behavior.

High-level architecture (summary):
- Control plane: route management, model catalog, policies, billing attribution, rollout manager.
- Data plane: serving runtime (GPU-optimized), KV/prefix caches, batching scheduler, kernel selection layer.
- Edge components: regional routers, autoscaling agents, telemetry aggregators.

Non-functional requirements and SLOs (contract with customers):
- Availability SLO (Dedicated): 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Latency SLO (hosted standard tier): P95 <= 200ms for short (<=256 token) requests; P95 <= 1200ms for 4k token horizon for supported models.
- Error budget policy: SLO burn triggers rollback to last stable rollout and paging to on-call.

Design tradeoffs and constraints:
- Kernel selection vs. model fidelity: aggressive quantization reduces cost but may impact generation quality for sensitive tasks — Optimize will surface quality-regression risk scores.
- Caching correctness: prefix caching introduces complexity for streaming and partial generation; default behavior is safe caching only for deterministic prompts unless customer opts-in.

Design doc snippets (example API contract):
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate
- Payload (JSON):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/unified-v2",
  "deployment_mode": "dedicated|hosted|private",
  "input": "<user prompt>",
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "stream": true,
  "route_policy": "lowest_latency"
}
```

4) Roadmap and themes (next two quarters)

Quarter A (next 8 weeks) - Themes: Reliability & Rollouts:
- Rollout manager GA: canary + automatic rollback, rollout analytics, owner isolation. (Owner: eng-platform)
- Routing engine stable release: support per-tenant policies, API + console. (Owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Observability: token-level cost attribution landed in Console. (Owner: eng-platform)

Quarter B (8–16 weeks) - Themes: Cost controls & enterprise readiness:
- Redwood Optimize v6: automated quantization recommendations with expected quality delta and one-click apply for Dedicated. (Owner: applied-ml-and-evals)
- Dedicated autoscaling policies: scheduled and workload-aware burst capacity. (Owner: eng-sre)
- Private deployment certificate automation and KMS integration. (Owner: eng-private-deployments)

Milestones and release cadence:
- Beta signups open after internal dogfood + ~2 weeks of customer pilot.
- Public launch (GA) targeted 2027-02-15 subject to pilot success and SRE readiness.

Dependencies and risks:
- Kernel performance regressions for new quantized kernels — mitigated by bench-suite and staging perf gates.
- Customer onboarding complexity for Private — mitigated by streamlining packaging and providing an on-prem quickstart.

5) Pricing and packaging notes

Principles:
- Usage-based pricing remains the default for Hosted.
- Dedicated: committed monthly/annual capacity contracts with unit pricing tied to GPU class and reserved vCPU/ram.
- Private: platform fee + optional support/installation services.

Proposed tiering (simplified):
- Hosted (Standard): pay-as-you-go per-token generation and per-embedding unit; tiered volume discounts at 50M, 200M tokens/month. Includes basic observability and community support.
- Hosted (Pro): higher throughput SLA, lower per-token price, dedicated routing priority.
- Dedicated (Reserved): base monthly fee for committed capacity + usage for burst; includes 99.9% uptime SLA, dedicated telemetry retention.
- Private (Enterprise): one-time platform/license fee + annual support; optional managed upgrades.

Pricing knobs to highlight in sales materials:
- Batching & caching advice from Optimize can change effective per-token price by 10–30% depending on workload. Provide examples in sales deck.
- Quantization profiles: conservative vs aggressive profiles with expected quality delta and cost estimates.

Example customer price note (copy for CS/Sales):
- "For a customer serving 150M tokens/month using batch-friendly embeddings, Optimize suggests batching + INT8 quantization delivering an estimated 22% cost reduction and 1.5x throughput improvement. Dedicated pricing with a 12-month commit reduces unit cost by an additional ~18%."

6) Q4 release notes and rollout plan (recent release: 2026 Q4 minor/major combined)

Release highlights:
- Routing engine: per-tenant policy rules, region fallback, and API for programmatic route updates.
- Optimize v5: batching suggestions + initial quantization profiles for two model families.
- Console: token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency histograms.

Bug fixes and performance improvements:
- Fixed a KV-cache eviction bug causing increased latencies for >2M small prompts (issue #SR-1248).
- Reduced cold-start kernel selection time by ~30% for Llama-family models.
- Improved autoscaler stability under burst workloads.

Rollout plan and canary stages:
1. Internal dogfood (week 0): all changes deployed to staging; run full regression & perf-suite.
2. Alpha customers (week 1–2): invited customers run pilot with dedicated SRE support; monitor P95 latency, error rates, and quality regressions against prompts.
3. Gradual canary (week 3–4): 10% -> 30% -> 100% of traffic for Hosted; Dedicated customers scheduled by account.
4. GA: announce in release notes, update docs and SDKs; enable sales enablement materials.

Operational runbook excerpts (if SLO breach occurs during rollout):
1) Pause rollout and freeze config changes.
2) Trigger automatic rollback to last stable release.
3) Open incident in PagerDuty, tag with rollout label, and notify product + eng-sre.
4) Collect traces and perf metrics; if root cause is a model/kernel regression, revert kernel selection policy.
